text: From the British garrison in Bathurst, armored paddle-steamers churned up the brown river, their brass guns glinting in the midday sun.
Colonial dispatches described Foday Kaba as an outlaw who refused customs taxes, tore down boundary stones, and gave sanctuary to runaway captives from neighboring territories.
When British envoys arrived at the mouth of the creek bearing treaties printed on parchment, Foday Kaba received them under the shade of a silk-cotton tree.
'You brought paper across the sea,' he told them calmly.
'We hold this soil by the bones of our fathers.
Paper does not grow in Kiang.'
